feed.title: NPR Topics: News
feed.subtitle: NPR news, audio, and podcasts. Coverage of breaking stories, national and world news, politics, business, science, technology, and extended coverage of major national and world events.

entry.title: Congress is under pressure to act on AI — here's what that could look like
entry.summary: Lawmakers are expressing broader willingness to regulate AI development, but the path forward may not be a quick one.

entry.title: DOJ charges Russian agents with plotting attacks, including in US
entry.summary: The indictment says the defendants belong to a network that "is one arm of the Russian Federation's apparatus used to carry out external attacks" worldwide.

entry.title: A tumultuous congressional primary season closes with record departures and defeats
entry.summary: Already, close to 100 lawmakers who started this Congress will not be around for the next one, according to an NPR analysis, driven by record-setting retirements and primary defeats.

entry.title: How Jared Kushner is mixing U.S. diplomacy with his billion-dollar business
entry.summary: The New Yorker's Dexter Filkins says while Trump's son-in-law is a U.S. special envoy negotiating peace, he's also working on private business deals, raising billions in some of the same countries.

entry.title: Mice with human brain cells offer a tool to study disease. Ethicists ask: What's next?
entry.summary: Neuroscientists have made a major advance in modeling the human brain in mice, offering a new way to study conditions like cerebral palsy. Ethicists ask if it changes how these mice should be treated.

entry.title: How are rising prices affecting you? NPR wants to know
entry.summary: Inflation, gasoline prices and the cost of living are top of mind in the election season. How are higher costs shaping the way you live? NPR wants to hear.

entry.title: Russia seizes Ukrainian POWs, then it demands favors from their relatives
entry.summary: Russia is believed to be holding thousands of Ukrainian POWs. Russia is also tormenting the families of these prisoners by contacting their relatives on social media and demanding they help Russia.

entry.title: Fed expected to raise interest rates. And, board votes to close Kennedy Center
entry.summary: The Fed is expected to raise interest rates today for the first time in three years. And, the Kennedy Center board voted yesterday to close the historic center.

entry.title: EU's Ursula von der Leyen says she wants Canada to become an associate member
entry.summary: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen on Wednesday proposed making Canada the European Union's first associate member, a striking overture as U.S. President Donald Trump's tariffs drive Ottawa closer to Europe.

entry.title: Senators question Trump's picks for top health positions, including surgeon general
entry.summary: On Wednesday, the Senate committee on health held a confirmation hearing for three top health officials, including surgeon general. Dr. Nicole Saphier is President Trump's third attempt to nominate a surgeon general.
